text:
Mia: Quick update from the scheduler workbench — we finished a wider canary of the compact-scheduler change and the numbers look solid across the fleet.

Jorge: Nice! top-line?

Mia: Summary: throughput +18% for short/med seq workloads, p99 latency down ~35ms (about -28% on our short-seq profiles), and estimated cost/token reduction ~12% after efficient batching kicks in. These are weighted averages across g4/g5 pools.

Priya: Any regressions observed?

Mia: Two small things: transient mem churn on a specific pod class (r5-highmem equivalent) during warmup — spike lasted ~45s and didn’t affect p50/p95. Also saw a handful of webhook timeouts that correlate to a monitoring sidecar upgrade — unrelated to the scheduler.

Anika: Can you paste the canary run IDs / queries we used so SRE can reproduce?

Mia: Canary run: compact-sched-v0.9-wide-1955; workload profile: short_chat_2026q1 + embedding_burst_small. Query set in the dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/bench/compact-sched-1955 (internal).

Mia: Config diff we pushed (high-level):
```
old:
  scheduler:
    packer: dynamic
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
new:
  scheduler:
    packer: compact
    max_batch_tokens: 3072
    micro_batch_threading: true
    token_window_prefetch: true
```

Ryan: SRE notes: we validated pod oom_kill = 0, no increase in node-level CPU steal, and infra cost delta is neutral. The mem churn looks like allocation pattern change — added a short lived GC knob to mitigate, will keep an eye.

Jorge: Did you run the fallback tests? i.e., if compact packer fails, does routing go back to the old packer?

Mia: Yes — rollout policy includes automatic fallback to packer=dynamic on error rate > 0.5% for 5m rolling window. No fallbacks triggered in canary.

Sam: Product/SDK callout: downstream clients may see slightly different tokenization alignment at the very tail of prompt concatenation due to different batch packing; we validated end-to-end outputs on the eval set but flagging for SDK teams.

Priya: How aggressive is the rollout? timeline?

Mia: Plan: tonight at 0200 UTC widen from 15% -> 50% of traffic for eligible clusters, then 2h hold and metrics check. If stable, 0800 UTC complete to remaining dedicated pools. Blocking items: SRE mitigation for the mem churn (Ryan) and a short validation on long-seq eval to ensure no p99 tail regression (Anika).

Anika: I'll run the long-seq regression suite in staging now, will post results in this thread within the hour.

DeployBot: deploy compact-scheduler/v0.9 triggered by @Mia. Canary targets: g4-prod-*, g5-prod-*, dedicated-small. Rollout id: rb-1955-compact.

Mia: Early ops note: if you see any unexplained latency blips in the next 4 hours add the tag "compact-sched-1955" to the incident so we can filter quickly.

Ryan: SRE follow-up: implemented a transient GC throttle to smooth allocation spikes; pushed a small agent hotfix. Will monitor memoryhist and pod_restarts dashboards.

Anika: Long-seq suite: p99 unchanged, p50 slightly improved. No correctness diffs on the eval prompts. Joining the rollout.

Mia: Thanks all. If we stay green on the 50% hold we'll proceed to full by 0800 UTC. Post-rollout I'll upload the full bench CSV and cost model updates.

Sam: Big win — can we get a concise blurb for the weekly product sync? 2 lines about throughput + cost.

Mia: Yep — will post a 2-line summary + link to dashboard once full rollout completes. :tada:
